mainTopic: Whether the מבול reached ארץ ישראל and the survival of the רימא, the names of בבל, and the משנה's exemptions for slaughtering the שעיר המשתלח and a רובע or נרבע outside the עזרה.
overview: This amud first finishes the dispute over whether the מבול came down on ארץ ישראל. רבי יוחנן says it did not, and ריש לקיש says it did. The גמרא tests both views against the question 'where are the dead of the מבול?' and against the פסוק 'everything on dry land died'. It also brings two versions of who attacked whom. רב חסדא's teaching that the flood waters were boiling explains how people could die even where the water did not reach. Next comes the giant רימא. It survived with only the tip of its nose inside the תיבה and its horns tied to the תיבה, and a miracle cooled the water around the תיבה. The גמרא then explains the names of בבל, מצולה and שנער, as hints that the dead of the מבול ended up there. Finally it returns to the משנה. It settles a contradiction about whether the שעיר המשתלח is fit to come to the אהל מועד by saying the line falls at the וידוי. It then opens a question about the source for exempting a רובע and a נרבע, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But the bones were already cleared away
steps.stepSummary: An objection: the dead of the מבול and of נבוכדנצר were already removed, so why worry about their graves?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they were already cleared away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the earlier discussion. If the bones of those dead were already removed, there should be nothing left to worry about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source treated hidden graves from the מבול and from נבוכדנצר as a reason to inspect a place, for example the place used for the פרה אדומה. The objection is that those bones were already removed, so the concern seems pointless.

phrases.english: But they were cleared away!
phrases.notes: 'They' means the bones of the dead, which were already removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section on the earlier source about inspecting for graves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The concern about hidden graves of the dead of the מבול and of נבוכדנצר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bones were already removed, no worry should remain.

steps.title: Cleared from ירושלים, but not from all of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The bones were removed only from ירושלים, so the worry still applies in the rest of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that they were cleared out of ירושלים, they were not cleared out of all of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by limiting it. The clearing happened only in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed the bones were removed everywhere. The answer says the removal covered ירושלים alone. Anywhere else in ארץ ישראל, hidden graves are still a real concern, so a place must be inspected.

keyTerms.meaning: granted that... (concedes a point before limiting it)

phrases.english: Granted that they were cleared out of Jerusalem,
from all of the Land of Israel they were not cleared out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bones were removed everywhere, so there is nothing to worry about.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were removed only from ירושלים. The rest of ארץ ישראל still needs inspection.
steps.whatToRemember: Bones removed from ירושלים does not mean bones removed from all of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Another version: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן from 'where are the dead'
steps.stepSummary: In the other version, ריש לקיש argues that the question 'where are the dead of the מבול and of נבוכדנצר?' puts both groups in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went the other way. ריש לקיש objected to רבי יוחנן: 'Where are the dead of the מבול? Where are the dead of נבוכדנצר?' Doesn't this mean that just as these were here, those were here too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the argument. Here ריש לקיש uses the same quote to attack רבי יוחנן's view that the מבול never reached ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote mentions the dead of the מבול and the dead of נבוכדנצר side by side. Everyone agrees that נבוכדנצר's victims died in ארץ ישראל. ריש לקיש reasons that because the two groups are listed together, the dead of the מבול must also have been in ארץ ישראל. That would mean the מבול came there.

keyTerms.meaning: נבוכדנצר, king of בבל, who killed many in ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: In this version the roles are reversed: ריש לקיש is the one attacking, and רבי יוחנן (who says the מבול did not reach ארץ ישראל) is defending.

phrases.english: There are those who say,
Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Where are the dead of the Flood?
Where are the dead of Nebuchadnezzar?
What, is it not that since these were here,
phrases.notes: 'These' are נבוכדנצר's victims, who certainly died in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: those too were here?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the discussion, with the attack now aimed at רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the מבול did not come down on ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Listing the two groups together suggests they share the same location, and נבוכדנצר's victims were in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The two groups are not comparable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that each group is as it is: one was in ארץ ישראל and the other was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the comparison. Being mentioned together does not mean the two groups died in the same place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's proof depended on treating the two groups as parallel. רבי יוחנן says each case stands on its own. נבוכדנצר's dead were in ארץ ישראל, while the dead of the מבול were not, because the מבול did not come there.

phrases.english: Are the cases comparable?!
This is as it is, and that is as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יוחנן against the objection of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the two groups are listed together, both must have been in ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each group is judged separately. Only נבוכדנצר's dead were in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The פסוק says everything on dry land died
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש argues from the פסוק 'everything on dry land died': if the מבול never reached ארץ ישראל, why did anyone there die?
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected again: 'Of all that was on the dry land, they died.' My view works fine: I say the מבול came down on ארץ ישראל, and that is why they died. But by your view, why did they die?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a second objection, this time from a פסוק. The פסוק says every creature on dry land died, including those in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says everything on dry land died, which should include ארץ ישראל. If the water covered ארץ ישראל, that is easy to explain. If it did not, as רבי יוחנן says, there seems to be no cause of death there.

keyTerms.meaning: it works well according to me

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
“Of all that was on the dry land, they died” —
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:22

phrases.english: It works well according to me, since I say
the Flood came down on the Land of Israel —
because of that they died.
But according to you, why did they die?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first objection was answered, ריש לקיש brings a new objection from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the מבול did not come down on ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says everything on dry land died. Without water in ארץ ישראל, there is no cause of death there.

steps.title: They died from the heat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the people of ארץ ישראל died from the heat of the flood waters, not from drowning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the heat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that people in ארץ ישראל could die without being flooded. The heat of the flood waters reached them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed drowning was the only way to die in the מבול. רבי יוחנן adds a second cause, the heat that came with the flood waters. That heat spread to ארץ ישראל even though the water did not.

phrases.english: Because of the heat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only water could have killed them, so the water must have reached ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The heat of the flood waters killed them, even without water reaching ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the flood waters were boiling
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's teaching supports the idea that the flood waters were hot. They sinned with heat and were punished with heat, as shown by comparing 'וישכו' with 'שככה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רב חסדא, who said: they sinned with heat and were punished with heat. Here it says 'and the waters calmed (וישכו)', and there it says 'and the king's anger calmed (שככה)'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's answer fits a known teaching of רב חסדא. That teaching says the flood waters were boiling hot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא compares the word for 'calmed' in the story of the מבול with the same word in מגילת אסתר, where it describes the king's hot anger cooling down. Because the word is used for something hot cooling down, the flood waters must have been hot too. That supports the claim that heat could kill people outside the area of the water.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the מבול did not cover ארץ ישראל. People there died from the boiling heat of the waters, as רב חסדא teaches from 'וישכו' and 'שככה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the פסוק 'everything on dry land died' does not prove the water itself reached ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: This is in line with Rav Ḥisda,
as Rav Ḥisda said:
With heat they sinned,
phrases.notes: 'Heat' here means burning passion: the generation of the מבול sinned through forbidden relations.

phrases.english: and with boiling water they were punished;
as it is written here: “And the waters calmed,”
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:1

phrases.english: and it is written there: “And the king’s anger calmed.”
phrases.notes: אסתר 7:10. The king's 'anger' is literally his heat, so the same word means something hot cooling down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer of step 6 with רב חסדא's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That the flood waters were hot enough to kill even where the water did not reach.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's comparison of 'וישכו המים' (בראשית) with 'וחמת המלך שככה' (אסתר).

steps.title: In another version, רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the words 'dry land'
steps.stepSummary: Some say the argument was the other way around. רבי יוחנן argues that the פסוק's words 'dry land' fit his view, since ארץ ישראל stayed dry, but they do not fit ריש לקיש's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went like this: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש from the פסוק 'everything on the dry land died.' For me, since I say the flood never came down on ארץ ישראל, it makes sense that there was dry land. But for you, what 'dry land' was there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the debate. This time רבי יוחנן is the one asking, and he uses the words 'dry land' against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, ריש לקיש used this פסוק to attack רבי יוחנן. Here the same פסוק is turned around: if the whole world was flooded, as ריש לקיש says, there was no dry land anywhere, so the פסוק's wording seems to support רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well according to my view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 5. There ריש לקיש used this פסוק to attack רבי יוחנן. In this version, רבי יוחנן uses the same פסוק to attack ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
"Of all that was on the dry land, died"
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:22

phrases.english: Granted, according to me, since I say
the flood did not come down on Eretz Yisrael,
because of that there was dry land.
But according to you, what is "dry land"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the debate, with the same פסוק now used against ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the flood covered ארץ ישראל too
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole world was flooded, no dry land was left, so the פסוק's phrase 'dry land' makes no sense.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: it means land that was dry before the flood
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that 'dry land' means land that had been dry at first, before the flood came.
steps.simpleTranslation: Land that was dry at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself. He says the פסוק calls it 'dry land' because of what it was before the flood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not say any land stayed dry during the flood. He reads 'dry land' as describing the land's earlier state, so the פסוק no longer proves that ארץ ישראל escaped the flood.

phrases.english: Land that was dry originally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Dry land' means land that stayed dry during the flood.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Dry land' means land that had been dry before the flood.

steps.title: Why mention 'dry land' at all? To teach that the fish were spared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק describes the land as dry at all. It answers with רב חסדא: the words 'dry land' teach that the decree was only on dry-land creatures, not on the fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק call it 'dry land'? It follows רב חסדא, who said: in the generation of the flood, no decree was made against the fish in the sea, as it says 'of all that was on the dry land, died,' and not the fish in the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק mentions 'dry land' if no land was dry during the flood. It answers that the words are there to exclude the fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the land by its earlier state still needs a reason. רב חסדא gives one: 'dry land' marks the difference between land creatures, who died, and sea creatures, who were not included in the decree. So the phrase does not mean any land stayed dry.
steps.whatToRemember: In this version, ריש לקיש reads 'dry land' as land that was dry before the flood. The פסוק uses the phrase to teach רב חסדא's rule that the fish were not part of the decree.

phrases.english: And why does it call it "dry land"?
It is like Rav Chisda's teaching.
As Rav Chisda said:
In the generation of the flood, no decree was made
against the fish in the sea,
as it says: "Of all that was on the dry land, died"
and not the fish in the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ חָרָבָה? כִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the פסוק uses the word 'dry land' at all, which completes ריש לקיש's answer in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the phrase teaches something else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'dry land' is there to tell us some land was dry during the flood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'dry land' is there to exclude the fish from the decree.

steps.title: How did the giant רימא survive if the flood covered ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The fact that the רימא survived is easy to explain for רבי יוחנן. But according to the view that the flood reached ארץ ישראל, where did the רימא survive, since it was far too big for the תיבה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for the one who says the flood did not come down on ארץ ישראל, that explains how the רימא survived there. But for the one who says it did come down, where did the רימא survive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that the flood reached ארץ ישראל. It asks how the huge רימא survived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רימא is too large to fit in נח's תיבה. If ארץ ישראל stayed safe, the רימא could have survived there. If the whole world was flooded, there seems to be no place where it could have survived.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
the flood did not come down on Eretz Yisrael,
that is how the reima survived there.
But according to the one who says it did come down,
where did the reima survive?
phrases.notes: The רימא was too huge to fit inside נח's ark.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא יָרַד מַבּוּל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge against the view that the flood reached ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the flood came down on ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רימא could not fit in the תיבה, so if every land was flooded it had no way to survive.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: young רימא were brought into the תיבה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that young רימא, which were small enough to fit, were brought into the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: they brought young ones into the תיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers the question about the רימא. Only the babies were brought into the תיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adult רימא were too big, but their young could fit inside. That way the species survived even if the whole world was flooded.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
They brought cubs into the ark.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: גּוּרִיּוֹת הִכְנִיסוּ בַּתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רימא question from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No רימא could have fit in the תיבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Young רימא were small enough to be brought into the תיבה.

steps.title: Even a one-day-old רימא was as big as a mountain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי with רבה בר בר חנה's report: he saw a one-day-old רימא as big as הר תבור, so even a baby could not have fit in the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבה בר בר חנה said: I myself saw a one-day-old רימא, and it was like הר תבור. How big is הר תבור? Forty פרסאות. Its neck was three פרסאות long, the resting place of its head was a פרסה and a half. It dropped dung and blocked the ירדן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי ינאי's answer. Even a newborn רימא was huge, far too big for the תיבה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי's answer depends on the young ones being small. רבה בר בר חנה's report says a baby only one day old was as big as a mountain, so the problem from step 11 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: פרסאות, a long unit of distance

phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say:
I myself saw
a one-day-old offspring of a reima,
phrases.notes: Some versions have בת in round brackets; the corrected wording is בר, in square brackets. Either way it means one day old.

phrases.english: and it was like Mount Tabor.
And how big is Mount Tabor?
Forty parasangs.
The length of its neck was three parasangs,
the resting place of its head was a parasang and a half.
It dropped dung and dammed up the Jordan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ינאי's answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's claim that young רימא fit in the תיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even a one-day-old רימא was as big as a mountain, so a young one could not fit in the תיבה either.

steps.title: Only the head of the רימא was brought into the ark
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the people in the תיבה brought in only the רימא's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They brought its head into the תיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new answer to the problem from Step 13. The whole baby רימא could not fit, so only its head was brought inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that even a newborn רימא was too big for the תיבה. רבי יוחנן answers that it did not need to be fully inside. Only its head was inside, and the rest of its body stayed out.

keyTerms.meaning: A giant wild animal, far too big to fit in the ark

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
They brought its head into the ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the size problem raised in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial-entry solution: the animal did not need to be fully inside.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since even a baby רימא could not fit, it could not have survived in the תיבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only its head was inside, and that was enough for it to survive.

steps.title: Even the head was too big
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with the report that the רימא's head alone covered a פרסה and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say that the spot where its head rests is a פרסה and a half?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's answer. It cites a report that the רימא's head was enormous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the head alone covered a פרסה and a half, it could never fit in the תיבה. So the answer that only the head went inside does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master", a respectful way of referring to an earlier speaker
The resting place of the head
A פרסה, a long distance of several miles

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
phrases.notes: "The Master" here is רבה בר בר חנה, the one who described the רימא in Step 13.

phrases.english: The resting place of its head is a parasang and a half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the רימא's head was brought into the תיבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The head alone was a פרסה and a half, far bigger than the תיבה.

steps.title: Only the tip of its nose was brought in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the answer: only the tip of the רימא's nose was brought into the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they brought the tip of its nose into the תיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבי יוחנן's answer. It makes the part inside much smaller, just the tip of the nose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that the רימא was only partly inside stays the same. What changes is the amount: instead of the whole head, only the very tip of the nose was inside. That is small enough to fit.

phrases.english: Rather, they brought the tip of its nose into the ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Revises Step 14 to answer the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the tip of the nose was inside.

steps.title: Why would רבי יוחנן need this answer at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needs to explain the רימא's survival this way, since he holds that the flood never reached ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say that the flood did not come down on ארץ ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled. According to רבי יוחנן's own opinion, the רימא could simply have survived in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the רימא's survival is easy to explain for רבי יוחנן, because ארץ ישראל stayed dry. So why does רבי יוחנן himself need the nose-in-the-תיבה answer?

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The flood did not come down on Eretz Yisrael!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבי יוחנן gave the answer in Steps 14 and 16 at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that רבי יוחנן offered the nose explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By his own view the רימא could have survived in dry ארץ ישראל, so he has no need for this answer.

steps.title: He was speaking according to ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן gave this explanation according to ריש לקיש's view, not his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the words of ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן was not giving his own opinion here. He was explaining how the רימא survived according to ריש לקיש, who holds that the flood did reach ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן himself, the רימא could have stayed in ארץ ישראל. But ריש לקיש holds that the flood came there too. So רבי יוחנן was showing how even ריש לקיש could explain the רימא's survival.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words or opinion of

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן changed his mind. He still holds that the flood did not reach ארץ ישראל. He is answering according to someone else's opinion.

phrases.english: He was saying it according to the words of Reish Lakish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statement is made according to another Amora's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's answer reflects his own position, so it seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was answering according to ריש לקיש's view, which needs this explanation.

steps.title: But the ark was moving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רימא's nose could stay in the תיבה when the תיבה was floating and moving.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תיבה was moving!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the nose answer. The תיבה floated around on the water, so how did the רימא keep its nose inside?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the nose inside works only if the רימא and the תיבה stay together. Since the תיבה kept moving, the רימא would be left behind.

phrases.english: But the ark was moving!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the nose answer from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tip of the רימא's nose was kept in the תיבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A moving תיבה would pull away from the רימא.

steps.title: They tied its horns to the ark
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the רימא's horns were tied to the תיבה, so it moved along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: They tied its horns to the תיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש solves the moving-תיבה problem. The רימא was tied to the תיבה by its horns, so wherever the תיבה went, the רימא went too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being tied by the horns keeps the רימא attached to the moving תיבה. That way its nose could stay inside the whole time.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They tied its horns to the ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רימא could not keep up with the moving תיבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its horns were tied to the תיבה, so it was pulled along.

steps.title: The flood waters were boiling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with רב חסדא's teaching that the flood generation was punished with boiling water. How could the רימא outside the תיבה survive?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חסדא say: The people of the דור המבול sinned with heat and were punished with boiling water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a bigger problem. Even if the רימא was tied to the תיבה, its body was in the flood water, and that water was boiling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא teaches that the flood water was boiling hot, as a fitting punishment. Any animal whose body was outside the תיבה should have been boiled to death. So tying the רימא to the תיבה does not explain how it survived.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chisda say:
The people of the generation of the flood sinned with boiling heat
and were punished with boiling water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the רימא survived while tied outside the תיבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The flood water was boiling, so anything in it should have died.

steps.title: That problem applies to the ark and to עוג too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if boiling water is a problem, how did the תיבה itself move through it, and how did עוג survive?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, how did the תיבה move? And also, how did עוג מלך הבשן survive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that it proves too much. If the boiling water is a problem for the רימא, it is just as much a problem for the תיבה and for עוג. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the תיבה made it through the boiling water, and that עוג survived the flood. So there must be some explanation for how things survived it. The boiling-water challenge cannot knock out only the רימא.

keyTerms.meaning: How did he stand, how did he survive

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, how did the ark move?

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, עוֹג מֶלֶךְ הַבָּשָׁן הֵיכָא קָאֵי?
phrases.english: And also, how did Og, king of the Bashan, survive?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-challenges the objection in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The boiling-water objection as a reason to reject only ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would also make it impossible for the תיבה and עוג to survive, yet they did.

steps.title: A miracle cooled the water by the ark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a miracle happened: the water around the sides of the תיבה cooled down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a miracle was done for them: the water cooled at the sides of the תיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. A miracle made the water next to the תיבה cool, so the תיבה, the רימא, and עוג all survived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flood water was boiling, but not right next to the תיבה. Since the רימא was tied to the תיבה and עוג was near it, they were in the cooled water. This one miracle answers all three problems at once.
steps.whatToRemember: The רימא survived with the tip of its nose inside the תיבה and its horns tied to it. A miracle cooled the boiling flood water around the sides of the תיבה, which also explains how the תיבה and עוג survived.

phrases.english: Rather, a miracle was performed for them,
that the waters cooled at the sides of the ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the resolution that Step 22 set up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Miracle that solves all the cases together.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The boiling flood waters would have destroyed the רימא, the תיבה, and עוג.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water around the sides of the תיבה was miraculously cooled.

steps.title: Even according to ריש לקיש, no flood dead remained in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that even if the flood came down on ארץ ישראל, ריש לקיש himself teaches that all the flood's dead ended up in בבל. So nothing should remain in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to ריש לקיש: fine, the flood came down on ארץ ישראל, but nothing of it stayed there! For ריש לקיש said: why is בבל called 'מצולה'? Because all the dead of the flood sank there. And רבי יוחנן said: why is it called 'שנער'? Because all the dead of the flood were shaken out there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's view by using his own teaching. He says all the flood's dead sank in בבל, so none should be left in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש held that the flood reached ארץ ישראל, which could mean dead bodies were left there. But his own explanation of the name מצולה says every flood victim sank in בבל. רבי יוחנן's explanation of שנער points the same way. So ריש לקיש's position seems to make no practical difference for ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, even if we accept that
The depths, a name for בבל
The people who died in the flood

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording. This is ריש לקיש, who said the flood reached ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי נָמֵי דְּיָרַד מַבּוּל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל;
phrases.english: granted that the flood came down on Eretz Yisrael,
but nothing of it remained there!
For Reish Lakish said:
Why is it called "Metzulah"?
phrases.notes: "It" means בבל. See ישעיהו 44:27.

phrases.english: Because all the dead of the flood sank there.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Why is it called "Shinar"?
Because all the dead of the flood were shaken out there.
phrases.notes: This plays on the word נער, "shake out," which is hidden inside the name שנער.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ נְהִי נָמֵי דְּיָרַד מַבּוּל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהָא לָא פָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the תיבה discussion back to ריש לקיש's view that the flood reached ארץ ישראל, and challenges what follows from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's position that the flood came down on ארץ ישראל, so its dead could be found there
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's own explanation of מצולה says all the flood dead sank in בבל, so none would be left in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Some bodies must have stuck in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is impossible that none of the bodies got stuck in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is impossible that some did not get stuck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: even if most bodies were swept to בבל, some must have stuck in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All the dead sank in בבל' describes what happened to most of them. Realistically, some bodies stayed stuck where they were, so ריש לקיש's view still matters.

phrases.english: It is impossible that some did not get stuck.
phrases.notes: He means that some of the bodies in ארץ ישראל must have stayed stuck in the ground there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the statement: 'all' means most, and some bodies stayed behind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every single flood victim ended up in בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some bodies certainly stuck in ארץ ישראל, so ריש לקיש's view still matters.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: שנער shakes out its rich
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives another explanation of the name שנער: the land shakes off its wealthy people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: why is it called שנער? Because it shakes out its rich people.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just explained the name שנער, it adds another explanation from רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word נער means that rich people in בבל get 'shaken out' of their wealth. This is a side teaching linked to the previous one by the same name.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Why is it called "Shinar"?
Because it shakes out its rich people.
phrases.notes: He means that the rich in בבל don't stay rich.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ שִׁנְעָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching set off by רבי יוחנן's explanation of the name שנער in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name שנער hints that בבל does not let its rich people stay rich.

steps.title: But we see rich people in בבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we can see rich people in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that there are rich people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו: real life seems to show rich people in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בבל always shook off its rich, there should be no rich people there. What people can plainly see seems to go against רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: But we see that there are rich people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's statement in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that בבל shakes out its rich
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People can see that there are rich people in בבל.

steps.title: The wealth does not last three generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the wealth in בבל does not last three generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not last three generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there are rich people in בבל, but their wealth does not last for three generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו did not mean that nobody in בבל is ever rich. He meant that wealth there does not stay in a family for long.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not last, does not continue

steps.whatToRemember: The names of בבל (מצולה, שנער) are read as hints: the flood's dead ended up there, and its wealth does not last.

phrases.english: It does not last three generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the original statement more carefully: it is about how long wealth lasts, not whether rich people exist.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There are never any rich people in בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are rich people in בבל, but their wealth fades within three generations.

steps.title: רבי אמי: Eating the dust of בבל is like eating one's ancestors
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that whoever eats the dust of בבל is like someone eating the flesh of his ancestors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: whoever eats from the dust of בבל is as if he eats the flesh of his ancestors.
steps.whatsHappening: Going back to the idea that the flood's dead ended up in בבל, רבי אמי says the dust there is like the flesh of one's ancestors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all the flood's dead sank in בבל, its soil is mixed with their remains. Everyone comes from those earlier generations, so this is like eating your own ancestors.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Whoever eats from the dust of Babylonia,
it is as if he eats the flesh of his ancestors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי כָּל הָאוֹכֵל מֵעֲפָרָהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the idea from step 24 that the flood's dead are in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the flood's dead are buried in בבל's soil, eating that dust is like eating one's ancestors.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same, with a second opinion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing as רבי אמי. A second opinion in it says eating the dust is like eating creeping creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: whoever eats from the dust of בבל is as if he eats the flesh of his ancestors. And some say: as if he eats שקצים and רמשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי אמי word for word. It also quotes another view in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא matches רבי אמי exactly, which backs up his teaching. The 'יש אומרים' view compares the dust to the creeping creatures that also died in the flood and ended up in that soil.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Whoever eats from the dust of Babylonia,
it is as if he eats the flesh of his ancestors.
And some say:
it is as if he eats forbidden creatures and creeping things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אמי's statement in step 29 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's teaching about the dust of בבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the same words, plus a second opinion ('יש אומרים')

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the שעיר המשתלח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next case, the שעיר המשתלח, to start discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The goat that is sent away (the שעיר המשתלח).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the side discussion about the flood and בבל and quotes the next words of the משנה. This line sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that someone who offers the שעיר המשתלח of יום כיפור outside the בית המקדש is exempt. Quoting these words opens a new topic in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement by an אמורא. It is a quote of the משנה's words, marking where the next discussion begins.

phrases.english: The scapegoat.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here: offering this goat outside the בית המקדש is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the flood and goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's case of the שעיר המשתלח, which is exempt when offered outside, so it can be discussed.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the scapegoat is fit to come to the Tent of Meeting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that excludes the שעיר המשתלח from שחוטי חוץ only because it is not 'for ה׳'. It assumes the goat IS fit to come to the entrance of the אהל מועד, which clashes with what was said before.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא asks whether the word 'offering' includes things given for Temple upkeep (בדק הבית), since they are also called an offering. It answers that the פסוק 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד' limits the law to things fit to come there, and Temple-upkeep items are not fit. It then asks whether the שעיר המשתלח stays included, since it IS fit to come there. It answers that the word 'to ה׳' takes it out, because it is not set aside for ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to argue with the previous source. That source treated the שעיר המשתלח as not fit to come to the אהל מועד, but this ברייתא says it is fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needs a separate word, 'לה׳', to take the שעיר המשתלח out of the איסור of שחוטי חוץ. It would only need that word if the goat passes the first test of being fit for the אהל מועד. So the ברייתא holds the goat IS fit, while our earlier source said it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: a source is brought that seems to clash with what was just said
Items given to הקדש for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the מזבח
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the place where קרבנות are brought
The פסוק teaches: introduces the word in the פסוק that settles the question

steps.confusionAlert: Both the earlier source and the ברייתא agree that you are not חייב for slaughtering the שעיר המשתלח outside. They only argue about the reason: is it not fit for the אהל מועד, or is it fit but not 'for ה׳'?

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Or from the word 'offering', I might understand
that it includes even items consecrated for Temple upkeep
since they are called an offering,
as it is said: 'And we have brought the offering of ה׳'?
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:50

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

phrases.english: meaning only something fit to come into the Tent of Meeting;
this excludes items consecrated for Temple upkeep
which are not fit.
I will exclude these, since they are not fit;
but I will not exclude the goat that is sent away,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לָבֹא אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד!
phrases.english: since it is fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting!
The verse teaches: 'to ה׳'
to exclude the goat that is sent away,
since it is not set aside for ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in connection with the משנה's case of the שעיר המשתלח, which was just quoted in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שעיר המשתלח is not fit to come to the entrance of the אהל מועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא needs the word 'לה׳' to exclude the goat only because it holds the goat IS fit for the אהל מועד. That directly contradicts the claim that it is not fit.

steps.title: Before the lottery versus after the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two sources talk about different times. The ברייתא means before the הגרלה, when the goat is still fit. The other source means after the הגרלה, when it is no longer fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is no problem. Here, the ברייתא is talking about before the lottery. There, the other source is talking about after the lottery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by splitting the two sources into two different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול draws lots to decide which goat goes to ה׳ and which goes to עזאזל. Before the הגרלה, either goat could still become a קרבן, so it counts as fit for the אהל מועד. After the הגרלה, the goat for עזאזל is no longer meant for the אהל מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the formula for answering a contradiction
The lottery on יום כיפור that decides which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
Here... there: each source is talking about a different case

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
here it is before the lottery,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא, which said the goat is fit.

phrases.english: there it is after the lottery.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן קוֹדֶם הַגְרָלָה, כָּאן לְאַחַר הַגְרָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised from the ברייתא in step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time (before versus after the הגרלה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources argue about whether the שעיר המשתלח is fit for the אהל מועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not argue. Before the הגרלה the goat is fit; after it, it is not.

steps.title: Even after the lottery the goat comes in for the confession
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. Even after the הגרלה, the שעיר המשתלח is still brought inside for the וידוי, so it should still count as fit for the אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the lottery too, the goat is fit, because there is still the confession said over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, saying it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on the goat no longer being fit after the הגרלה. But the כהן גדול still says וידוי over the שעיר המשתלח inside the עזרה after the lottery. So even after the הגרלה the goat still comes to the entrance of the אהל מועד, and the contradiction is back.

keyTerms.meaning: The confession the כהן גדול says over the שעיר המשתלח on יום כיפור
But there is: points to a fact that breaks the previous answer

phrases.english: After the lottery too, it is fit,
since there is still the confession!
phrases.notes: He means the כהן גדול confesses over the goat in the עזרה after the lottery, so it still comes inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that after the הגרלה the שעיר המשתלח is no longer fit for the אהל מועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The וידוי is still said over the goat inside after the הגרלה, so it is still brought to the אהל מועד and should still count as fit.

steps.title: Before and after the confession
steps.stepSummary: רב מני answers that the dividing line is the וידוי, not the הגרלה. Before the וידוי the goat is fit for the אהל מועד. After the וידוי it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב מני said: It is not difficult. Here it is before the confession, there it is after the confession.
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer, which split the time at the הגרלה, did not work. רב מני gives a new answer that splits the time at the וידוי instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 34 showed that the goat is still brought inside after the הגרלה, because the וידוי happens inside. So רב מני moves the line later, to the moment the וידוי is finished. The ברייתא speaks of the time before the וידוי, when the goat is still fit. The other source speaks of the time after it, when the goat is never brought in again.

keyTerms.meaning: The confession said over the שעיר המשתלח
It is not difficult; the two sources do not clash
Here... there; each source speaks of a different case or time

steps.whatToRemember: The שעיר המשתלח counts as fit for the entrance of the אהל מועד until its וידוי is done. After that it is no longer fit.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Mani said:
It is not difficult;
here, it is before the confession,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that treats the goat as fit to come to the entrance.

phrases.english: there, it is after the confession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב מַנִּי: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from step 33, which step 34 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time (two different stages of the goat's process)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line is the הגרלה, so the goat would be unfit right after the lottery.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line is the וידוי. Until the וידוי is done the goat still goes inside, so it is fit. After that it is not.

steps.title: The next case in the משנה: רובע and נרבע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, an animal that was a רובע or a נרבע. It does this to start discussing that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal that copulated with a person, and an animal that was the object of bestiality.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new case in the משנה. It quotes the words here to set up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an animal cannot be brought as a קרבן, so a person who slaughters it outside is exempt. The quote opens a new discussion about which words in the פסוק teach this exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that actively mated with a person
An animal that a person mated with

phrases.english: An animal that copulated with a person, and an animal that was the object of bestiality.
phrases.notes: This is a short quote. The full משנה line says one who slaughters these outside is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the שעיר המשתלח topic and moves to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who slaughters a רובע or a נרבע outside the עזרה is exempt, because it is not fit to be a קרבן.

steps.title: Why not learn it from 'the entrance of the אהל מועד'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the exemption for a רובע or a נרבע needs its own source. It could be learned from the words 'פתח אהל מועד', the same words used for the cases before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this too, derive it from 'the entrance of the Tent of Meeting'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source for this exemption. It suggests that the earlier words of the פסוק already cover this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier cases in the משנה were exempt because they are not fit to come to the entrance of the אהל מועד. A רובע or a נרבע is also not fit to be brought there. So why does the משנה need a different part of the פסוק for it?

keyTerms.meaning: Let me derive it; why not learn it from this source?
The entrance of the אהל מועד; words from the פסוק about slaughtering outside

phrases.english: And this too, let me derive it
from 'the entrance of the Tent of Meeting'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא נָמֵי תִּיפּוֹק לִי מִפֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which words of the פסוק teach the exemption quoted in step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source the משנה gives for exempting a רובע and a נרבע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A רובע or a נרבע is not fit to come to the entrance of the אהל מועד. So the words 'פתח אהל מועד', which taught the earlier exemptions, should cover this case too. That makes a separate source seem unneeded.
